definition: In psychometric assessment, a first-order factor is a directly measured dimension in a factor model, represented here as one of several correlated factors used to explain patterns in interview scale scores. A first-order factor model means the observed ratings are organized into these primary factors without adding a higher-level factor above them.

reasons: The packet supports only that a first-order factor model with four correlated factors fit the interview data; it does not define a first-order factor as a directly measured dimension.
The statement that observed ratings are organized into primary factors without a higher-level factor is not established by the packet and goes beyond the cited model description.
The definition adds psychometric/general explanatory claims that are broader than the source evidence and are not supported as a definitional sense of the term.
The packet does not support the claim that a “first-order factor” is a “directly measured dimension” (no definition of first-order factor is provided).

The definition’s framing about explaining “patterns in interview scale scores” is not explicitly stated in the packet (the packet reports a factor structure and model fit, but not this interpretive wording).

The definition states that a first-order factor model “means the observed ratings are organized into these primary factors without adding a higher-level factor above them.” The packet does not mention or contrast the presence/absence of a higher-level factor (e.g., no description of higher-order factors).
While the packet mentions “a first-order factor model with four correlated factors,” it does not provide enough detail to substantiate the additional specific characterization used in the definition.
